plan: Store the input dictionary as a deep copy and treat it as a composite tree: workspaces, sections, and groups hold ordered child lists; notes and references are leaves.
Implement total_word_count as a recursive aggregation that strips exact-form [[?ident]] markers from note text before counting \b\w+\b runs, and takes a reference's declared word_count.
Implement unresolved_markers as a recursive collection into a set (marker identifiers from note text plus each reference's unresolved list), returned sorted lexicographically.
Implement outline as a deterministic preorder traversal emitting the workspace title, then '<kind>: <title>' lines indented two spaces per nesting level in list order.

Implement move with full validation before any mutation: string-type ids, item lookup, destination resolution ('workspace' literal or section/group id), container-kind check, insertion-index bounds check, and a subtree scan rejecting moves of a container into itself or a descendant; only then pop and insert, so failed moves leave the data untouched.
Return deep copies from to_data so callers cannot mutate internal state.
mechanisms: Composite tree of heterogeneous items with containers (section/group) and leaves (note/reference)
Uniform recursive dispatch on item kind shared by all summary operations
Recursive aggregation for total word count with marker-stripping tokenization for notes and declared counts for references
Set-based recursive marker collection with sorted output
Deterministic preorder traversal with depth-based two-space indentation for the outline
Containment invariant enforcement: container-only destinations plus no self/descendant cycles
Atomic move via validate-everything-then-mutate ordering, guaranteeing failed moves leave to_data unchanged
